Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to migrate their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS will make app replacement easier

Although it's not common, developers will occasionally take down an existing app and launch a new app to replace it, requiring users to switch to another standalone app.

Even though most developers try to make the transition as smooth as possible, when it comes to data that isn't stored in the cloud, the migration process still requires some effort from users.

In iOS 27.2, Apple will address this with a new, system-managed migration process that can transfer an app's data and supported settings to its designated replacement app before deleting the old app.

Based on the current code in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

"The developer suggests migrating the data and settings of your existing '%1$@' app to the new '%2$@' app. Your iPhone can now do this for you, and then you can start using the new app. When finished, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone."

Users can then choose to "Migrate App Data & Settings" or "Don't Migrate Anything." If users decline the migration, iOS will display a second confirmation prompt, warning that some preferences (including notification and location settings) may need to be reconfigured.

To be clear, this feature appears to be limited to developers replacing their own apps with a designated successor app, and does not allow data to be migrated between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a number of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, location, and health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Individual app "Do Not Disturb" and "Focus Mode" settings
  • App Lock and protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and accessory Live Activities
  • Access permissions for related accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll continue to monitor changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report back if there's more information on how developers can implement it.
